title: Vendor Minimal Data Footprint & Live Redaction Exhibit (template)
content:
Purpose: This exhibit defines the minimum contractual and technical controls required from a vendor that provides inference, routing, or auxiliary services which process live customer queries. The objective is to guarantee a minimal data footprint during runtime, provide deterministic live redaction/masking behavior for sensitive attributes, and allow the customer to audit and verify controls without exposing production data.

Scope: Applies to any third-party vendor or subcontractor ("Vendor") that will, in any operational mode, accept requests containing customer data that could include personal data, credentials, secrets, or other sensitive information. This exhibit is intended to be attached to the Master Services Agreement or Data Processing Agreement where applicable.

Definitions: "Live Redaction" - deterministic removal or transformation of sensitive tokens or spans from request payloads and intermediate runtime caches prior to any persistent storage. "Transient KV Cache" - in-memory or on-host key-value cache used to accelerate inference (e.g., prefix caches, session caches). "Non‑Indexed Audit Trace" - time-limited operational logs that support debugging without retaining raw customer content.

Vendor Obligations (contractual):
- Minimal Footprint Standard: Vendor shall not persist original request content outside of ephemeral runtime memory unless explicitly authorized in writing. Any persistence must be documented, scannable, and time-limited to the minimum necessary for debugging (see Retention below).
- Live Redaction Requirement: For all supported input channels, Vendor must implement live redaction that masks or removes predefined sensitive categories (PII, secrets, payment data, health data) before any file, disk, or long-term log write. The redaction must be reproducible and verifiable via test vectors provided by Customer.
- Redaction Policy Publication: Vendor will provide a machine-readable redaction policy (JSON or YAML) that enumerates patterns, named entity classes, and transformation rules. The policy shall be maintained in the Vendor's evidence portal and versioned.

Technical Controls (minimum):
- Deterministic Masking: Vendor must support both token-level redaction (mask entire token) and span-level replacement (e.g., replace detected SSNs with "[REDACTED_SSN]"). The mapping between original and redacted tokens must not be retained.
- Multi-layer Detection: At minimum, live redaction must combine: 1) high‑precision regex patterns, 2) ML-based NER for named PII classes, and 3) heuristics for common structured formats (credit cards, emails).
- Policy Prioritization & Overrides: Customer-supplied allowlists/denylist rules take precedence. Vendor must provide a mechanism for per-customer policy overrides scoped to the customer's account or project.
- Hotpath Handling & Latency: Redaction must execute on the request hotpath with an SLA-bound latency impact (e.g., added < 20ms p50). Performance baselines and test harnesses shall be agreed in SOW/Annex.

Ephemeral Storage & KV Cache Requirements: 
- Transience Guarantee: Any KV cache or runtime cache that stores derived/request fragments must expose a retention configuration with a default TTL \u2264 30 seconds for production. For debug sessions the vendor may permit longer TTLs only with explicit Customer approval and must log the approval.
- No Persistent Indexes: Vendor shall not create searchable indexes of raw request content. Aggregated metrics (token counts, error rates) are permitted, provided they cannot be reverse-engineered into user content.
- Secure Memory Hygiene: Vendor must implement secure zeroing of in-memory buffers on eviction and protect caches with OS-level protections (mmap protections, no core dumps). Evidence of implementation must be included in onboarding checklist.

Logging, Observability & Auditability:
- Non-Content Operational Logs: Vendor logs must avoid raw request content. Where necessary, logs may include redaction hashes (non-reversible) and metadata (request ID, model version, latency).
- Non-Indexed Audit Traces: For debugging, Vendor may create time-limited traces that contain partial context; retention must be <= 7 days by default and must be configurable per-customer with clear approval workflow.
- Attestation & Evidence: Vendor shall provide quarterly attestations describing redaction coverage, results of internal redaction tests, and a summary of any exceptions. Attestations must include: the versioned redaction policy, example test vectors used, and high-level metrics (false-positive/false-negative rates).

Testing & Acceptance Criteria:
- Baseline Test Suite: Vendor must accept and execute a baseline test suite (provided by Customer) containing synthetic and red-team style test vectors that exercise edge cases (nested JSON with secrets, unicode obfuscation, HTML-escaped secrets, concatenated tokens).
- Blackbox Penetration Test: Annually, or on substantive redaction-policy changes, a third-party penetration test focused on data leakage must be performed; results provided to the Customer under NDA.
- Pass/Fail: Acceptance requires: 1) zero instances of raw sensitive tokens found in persisted stores during test runs, 2) demonstrable redaction on live requests issued via test harness, and 3) documented remediation plan for any detected gaps.

Incident Response & Forensics:
- Live Leakage Escalation: If a real-world leakage of raw sensitive content is suspected or detected, Vendor must immediately (within 2 hours) isolate impacted systems, suspend persistence, and notify Customer per the SLA notification timeline.
- Forensic Proofs: Vendor must provide immutable evidence (hashes of relevant memory snapshots, redaction policy versions, request identifiers) and a step-by-step timeline of the handling. Forensics must be limited to the smallest scope required; Customer may request escrowed artifacts under specific conditions.

Compliance, Certifications & Liability:
- Certifications: Vendor should maintain SOC2 Type II or equivalent and provide SOC2 scoping documentation that explicitly includes runtime redaction components.
- Liability: Vendor accepts contractual obligations for failures in redaction where negligence or failure to follow the redaction policy directly results in exposure. Specific indemnity and liability caps remain governed by the primary agreement.

Governance & Change Control:
- Policy Change Window: Vendor must notify Customer at least 30 days before any change to the redaction policy that could affect detection coverage. Emergency changes to fix vulnerabilities may be applied immediately but require post-change notice within 48 hours.
- Versioning & Rollback: Redaction policy artifacts must be versioned in VCS and support automatic rollback to any prior version used during a customer-specified timeframe.

Appendix A — Example Redaction Policy Snippets (illustrative):
- JSON policy example (conceptual):
  - pattern_class: SSN
    regex: "\\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\\b"
    transform: "[REDACTED_SSN]"
  - pattern_class: EMAIL
    ml_ner_fallback: PERSON_EMAIL
    transform: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"

Appendix B — Sample Test Cases: 
- Nested JSON: request body contains {"profile": {"bio": "Contact me at user(at)company[dot]com"}} -> must redact email-like tokens and unicode obfuscations.
- Concatenated tokens: "card: 4242424242424242expiry" -> detection must separate numeric sequences and redact.
- Multi-lingual leakage: PII in non-Latin scripts must be detected by language-aware NER or flagged for manual review.

Operational Notes & References:
- Include links to Confluence runbooks (confluence:Security-Runbooks/Live-Redaction) and the customer onboarding checklist (confluence:Vendor-Onboarding/Redaction).
- See Jira SEC-4217 for outstanding action items and PR GH-2384 for production redaction policy storage implementation.

Negotiation Guidance (for Legal teams):
- Consider binding a short SLA for redaction metrics (coverage % over baseline test vectors) with cure periods for deviations.
- Use the exhibit to carve out explicit allowed debug exceptions and require pre-approved change requests for any exception.

Notes for internal reviewers: This template is intended to be adaptable: tighten TTLs and retention, or expand detection requirements based on customer sensitivity. For high-regulated customers (finance, healthcare), attach a stricter annex that requires immediate deletion of any transient artifacts and more frequent third-party attestations.

Document history: Draft prepared by Ava Chen; initial review by Security Compliance (Diego Rivera). Next steps: circulate to Product Security and Contracts for SOW alignment.
